newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-ACID TEST FOR FOREST'S NEW RECRUITS.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-ACID TEST FOR FOREST'S NEW RECRUITS.

text.p: Nottingham Forest will find out if their week-long spending spree has brought them value for money when their new recruits face buoyant Liverpool on Saturday in the English premier league.
Relegation-threatened Forest started the week by signing Pierre van Hooydonk from Scottish giants Celtic for an initial 3.0 million pounds ($4.8 million).
The tall Dutch striker made his debut at Blackburn on Tuesday and, although he failed to find the net, Forest scored only their second goal in eight matches to earn a precious 1-1 draw.

On Thursday Forest clinched a deal with promising Tranmere striker Ian Moore for a further 1.0 million pounds ($1.6 million) and looked set to lure former England winger Chris Waddle back into the premier league on a free transfer.

In the event, Waddle's current club Bradford blocked the move -- at least for the time being -- robbing English fans of the chance of seeing the mesmerising 36-year-old trade tricks with his present-day equal in the England side, Liverpool's Steve McManaman.
Forest turned from Waddle back to Celtic on Friday in a bid to secure their third signing of the week in the shape of versatile Scottish international defender Brian O'Neil.
A deal had not been reached by 1230 GMT but general-manager Dave Bassett appeared ready to throw O'Neil into Saturday's home tie before the ink of his signature had dried on his contract.
Such is Forest's thirst for premier league points. They are currently 18th in the 20-team division and if the two sides below them win their games in hand they will be rock bottom.
In contrast, Liverpool are right back in the title race following Manchester United's surprise defeat at Sunderland last Saturday and their own stunning 4-3 win over Newcastle two days later.

Roy Evans's side are virtually injury-free and if they play like they did in the first half against Newcastle they should sweep past a Forest side which looked woefully short of ideas last weekend when they succumbed 2-0 to Arsenal without a fight.
Evans has to decide whether to play striker Stan Collymore bearing in mind the fiercely hostile reception he received at his former club when he returned for the corresponding fixture last season.
Collymore was given a police escort in and out of the City Ground and received a death-threat letter from Forest supporters who felt he betrayed their side by breaking his contract to join Liverpool.
Ian Woan is ready to return to the left side of Forest's midfield after suspension and illness but Chris Bart-Williams and Chris Allen are still injured.

The clash brings together England's two most successful European Cup sides. Liverpool won back-to-back Cups in 1977 and 1978 and Forest equalled the feat in the following two seasons before Liverpool claimed it back in 1981 and won it again in 1984.
But for English supporters it is a domestic cup clash between the two sides which remains firmly planted in the nation's collective memory.
Forest and Liverpool were the two sides whose F.A. Cup semifinal in 1989 ended in appalling tragedy when 96 spectators were crushed to death at Hillsborough stadium.
